headline: Closed hearing and set conditions for 109 North Street project; continued reviews for Brook Street Culvert and 11 Cross Street.
summary: The Conservation Commission closed the hearing on a Notice of Intent for 109 North Street and set order of conditions including a no-mow restriction and partial waiver of the 50-foot no-disturb zone. It continued several Notices of Intent, enforcement orders, and violation matters to later dates, issued certificates of compliance for three properties, approved two emergency tree-removal certifications, and discussed public meeting procedures without taking a final vote.

CITY OF METHUEN 
CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
Minutes of a Meeting – August 6, 2026 
 
 
The City of Methuen Conservation Commission held a hybrid meeting via in-
person and Zoom video conferencing (VC) on August 6, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. at 
Searles Building, 41 Pleasant Street, 2nd Floor Conference Room, Methuen, MA 
01844.  Present for this meeting were Dave Di Zazzo, Chair; Cara Seaman, Vice 
Chair; Kenneth Sateriale, Secretary; Rachel Lecher, Commissioner; and Patrice 
Friant, Commissioner.  Also present were Chris Parsons, Conservation Officer, and 
Michelle Davidson, Conservation Clerk.  Commissioner Sandra Bouleywas absent. 
Chairman Dave Di Zazzo announced that, pursuant to Chapter 20 of the Acts of 
2021, this meeting was conducted via remote means in accordance with applicable 
law.  Members of the public body, as well as members of the public, were able to 
access the meeting via virtual means through Zoom video conferencing.  In the 
event that access and participation were not achieved, the Commission would post 
on the City of Methuen website an audio or video recording, transcript, or other 
comprehensive record of proceedings as soon as possible after the meeting. 
 
 
PUBLIC HEARING 
 
1.  NOTICES OF INTENT: 
 
2. NOTICES OF INTENT CONTINUED: 
 
A.  Notice of Intent – DEP File #219-1323, MCC File #26-004 – 109 North Street 
– Andover Consultants, Inc.  – Nolberto Galicia (Continued from July 16, 2026)
Page 2 
 
Dennis Grecci of Andover Consultants appeared before the Commission and 
presented a revised site plan reflecting changes made in response to Commission 
discussion and peer review comments.  Key updates included a reduction of 
permanent and temporary impacts within the buffer zone by repositioning the 
house and tightening grading and landscaping plans.  All pavers were removed 
from the 50-foot no-disturb zone.  The post-and-rail fence was replaced with posts 
and conservation markers along the 50-foot line in sensitive areas, per Commission 
preference.  Remaining permanent impacts are limited to two green-hatched areas 
(left and right sides of the house) within the 50-to-35-foot buffer zone. 
Peer reviewer Maria Johnsenberg of Tighe & Bond confirmed that plan updates 
were consistent with prior discussion and that outstanding peer review comments 
had been addressed.  Recommended conditions, including no pesticides or 
herbicides in no-disturb zone areas, were noted as agreeable to the applicant. 
Commission discussion focused on the tightness of the site, the importance of 
maintaining the 50-foot no-disturb boundary, and preventing future encroachment 
through mowing.  Chair Di Zazzo expressed a preference for posts with markers 
over post-and-rail fencing in critical areas, and for prohibiting any mowing beyond 
the 50-foot line. 
No public comment was received. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Seaman to close the hearing.  Seconded by Friant.  All 
in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  Hearing closed. 
The Order of Conditions to include no-mow restriction beyond 50-foot line in all 
impacted areas; no pesticides or herbicides in no-disturb zone; posts with 
conservation markers at 50-foot boundary; partial waiver of 50-foot no-disturb 
granted for two limited areas. 
 
B.  Notice of Intent – DEP File #219-1324, MCC File #26-005 – Brook Street 
Culvert – TEC, Inc. – Department of Public Works, City of Methuen 
(Continued from July 16, 2026) 
 
Applicant requested continuation to allow time to respond to peer review 
comments.  Conservation Officer noted that he attended a meeting that was held 
during the week with the applicants and Maria Johnsenberg to resolve a 
discrepancy in the wetland boundary.  A revised plan with the corrected wetland 
line and new recreation area is forthcoming. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Seaman to continue to August 20, 2026.  Seconded by 
Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
C.  Notice of Intent – DEP File #219-1320, MCC File #26-001 – 11 Cross Street – 
Dresser, Williams & Way, Inc.  – CROSSLD QOZB, LLC
Page 3 
(Continued from July 16, 2026) 
 
Steven Dresser of Dresser, Williams & Way, Inc., appeared before the 
Commission on behalf of CROSSLD QOZB, LLC.  At the prior meeting, the 
Commission found the proposed plan did not meet the standards required to permit 
alteration within the 50-to-35-foot zone for emergency access.  A revised plan was 
submitted featuring a hammerhead turnaround (previously approved in concept by 
the fire department) to replace the loop design, keeping all construction outside the 
50-foot no-disturb zone. 
Additional changes included elimination of the subsurface detention system near 
the 50-foot zone, replaced with catch basins, a manhole, and a constructed wetland.  
A retaining wall and visual barrier (post-and-rail or fence) were added along the 
retaining wall area.  Reduction of floodplain fill was achieved, with compensatory 
areas relocated outside the 50-foot zone. 
Maria Johnsenberg of Tighe & Bond confirmed the hammerhead redesign largely 
addresses outstanding buffer zone concerns.  Final stormwater design is still 
needed for peer review completion. 
Applicant indicated intent to appear before the Community Development Board 
the following Wednesday and estimated a full submission to Maria by the first 
meeting in October.  Filing deadline was confirmed as September 21, 2026. 
MOTION: Motion made by Seaman to continue to October 1, 2026.  Seconded by 
Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
 
REGULAR PUBLIC MEETING 
 
3. CALL TO ORDER: 7:25 p.m. 
 
4. ACCEPTENCE OF THE AGENDA / AMENDMENTS (IN ANY): 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Sateriale to accept the agenda.  Seconded by Friant.  
All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
5. ACCEPTANCE OF MINUTES – July 16, 2026 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Sateriale to accept the minutes of July 16, 2026.  
Seconded by Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
6. NEW BUSINESS: 
 
5.  OLD BUSINESS:
Page 4 
A.  Stormwater Permit Application – 11 Cross Street – CROSSLD QOZB, LLC – 
Dresser, Williams & Way, Inc. 
Discussed in conjunction with Notice of Intent Item III-C above. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Seaman to continue to October 1, 2026.  Seconded by 
Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
B.  Enforcement Order #25-006 – 2 Muirfield Lane (Continued from June 4, 2026) 
 
Conservation Officer Chris Parsons reported that arborvitae have been removed 
and relocated to the proper area.  The owner was advised to contact Maureen 
Herald of Norse Environmental Services regarding planting mix.  Maureen was 
scheduled to conduct spot grade inspection the following week.  Owner is ahead of 
schedule and largely in compliance. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Seaman to continue to August 20, 2026.  Seconded by 
Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
C.  Notice of Violation #24-008 / Enforcement Order #25-001 – 25 Thayer Street – 
Moskal and Cavarallo (Continued from June 18, 2026) 
 
Conservation Officer reported that the property has been sold.  Mr. Parsons visited 
the site and spoke with the new owner's nephew, providing a business card and 
explaining that under Massachusetts statute, new owners automatically assume 
liability for existing violations.  Follow-up contact was expected; if no response by 
mid-week, Mr. Parsons would revisit the property.  A new enforcement order can 
be issued to the new owner as needed.  Remaining compliance items include 
installation of markers and posts. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Seaman to continue to August 20, 2026.  Seconded by 
Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
D.  Notice of Violation #25-016 – 46 Ayer Street (Continued from June 4, 2026) 
 
Matter requires monitoring through two growing seasons.  Site was noted to be in 
compliance at this time. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Seaman to continue to October 1, 2026.  Seconded by 
Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
E.  Notice of Violation #26-007 – 8 Grandview Road – William Kannan 
(Continued from June 18, 2026)
Page 5 
Mr. Parsons reported speaking with the owner; site is largely in compliance, 
materials removed, and vegetation is regrowing.  Site photos were reviewed by the 
Commission. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Seaman to continue to October 1, 2026.  Seconded by 
Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
F.  Notice of Violation #26-008 – 28 West Street (Continued from July 2, 2026) 
 
Mr. Parsons reported visiting the site.  The owner hand-sifted all dirty fill 
(Commission granted this administrative approach as an alternative to full 
removal).  Dirty fill and most of the illegal drainage pipe have been removed.  A 
small depression remains; owner wishes to fill and level the area, which is outside 
the conservation zone.  The owner was directed to apply for an RDA.   
 
MOTION: Motion made by Seaman to continue to October 1, 2026.  Seconded by 
Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
G.  Notice of Violation #26-010 – 14 Freeport Street – Wilfred Cyr 
 
Commission received a complaint regarding fill being pushed into wetlands by 
machinery.  A mound of fill was found within approximately 20 feet of an 
intermittent stream.  Owner was confirmed to be already in compliance regarding 
fill removal. 
Owner was directed to install 4x4 posts with conservation markers every 20 feet 
along the boundary line, starting at the corner.  Conservation markers are supplied 
free of charge by the Commission; owner is responsible for post installation.  Mr. 
Parsons to inspect when complete.  Matter to be monitored for two growing 
seasons; owner does not need to attend every meeting. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Seaman to continue to September 3, 2026.  Seconded 
by Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
H.  Request for Certificate of Compliance- File #219-1255, MCC File #21-003 – 
602 Lowell Street – Richard Giuffrida 
 
Applicant submitted as-built plan with certification letter and engineer's stamp.  
Work was confirmed complete and in compliance. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Seaman to issue Certificate of Compliance.  Seconded 
by Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.
Page 6 
I. Request for Certificate of Compliance DEP File #219-1313, MCC File #25-001 
– 65 Ormonde Road – Christina Stonionis 
 
Conservation Officer confirmed that the site is in compliance. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Seaman to issue Certificate of Compliance.  Seconded 
by Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
J. Request for Certificate of Compliance DEP File #219-1250, MCC File #20-009 
– 33/47R Danton Drive – 47R Danton Landowner, LLC 
 
Applicant provided an update on drainage system installation, sediment removal 
(approximately 3 tons removed), and pipe cap status.  Outstanding item: confirm 
status of two cleanouts and associated pipe shown on record plans (determined not 
to be present; pipe capped for future extension).  Applicant to submit complete as-
built documentation.  Informal filing deadline extended to Tuesday (August 11) 
given proximity to the standard August 10th deadline. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Seaman to continue to August 20, 2026.  Seconded by 
Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
K. Emergency Certification #26-011 – 80 Hampstead Street 
 
During a drainage inspection, a hazardous tree was identified and removed on-site.  
Tree split at the base and posed a direct threat to the structure. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Seaman to issue Emergency Certificate.  Seconded by 
Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
L.  Emergency Certification #26-012 – 64 Maple Street 
 
Conservation Officer noted this will be the last emergency certificate processed 
under the current procedure.  Going forward, all emergency certification requests 
will follow the DEP-recommended process via open.gov, requiring a joint 
inspection by the Health Department and Conservation Officer prior to issuance. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Seaman to issue an Emergency Certificate.  Seconded 
by Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
Beaver Management Policy Clarification 
Following discussion regarding a beaver dam situation on Stonewall, the 
Commission reaffirmed its policy: the Commission will breach dams as a courtesy 
measure only.  Trapping of beavers is the responsibility of the homeowner, who
Page 7 
must hire a licensed trapper.  The Commission confirmed this is consistent with 
Health Department guidance and standard practice – the Commission is not in the 
trapping business. 
 
8. CONSERVATION OFFICER'S REPORT:  
 
 Public Meeting Policy Discussion: 
 
Conservation Officer Chris Parsons and the Commission discussed proposed 
changes to meeting procedures, as clarified by the City Solicitor: 
Public Hearing vs.  Public Meeting Distinction 
Public Hearings (Notices of Intent): Any member of the public may speak.  The 
Commission is not obligated to respond.  A 3-minute rule may be applied; the 
board may vote to extend by up to 2 minutes for relevance. 
Regular Public Meetings: Open to public observation only.  The board has 
discretion to permit public comment but is not required to do so. 
 
3-Minute Public Comment Rule: 
 
Commissioner Sateriale reported that Community Development Director Jack 
Wilson confirmed via voicemail that a 3-minute public comment rule is commonly 
used, legally permissible, and may be adopted by a majority vote of the 
Commission.  A 2-minute extension may be granted by board majority vote.  New 
procedures may be noted on agendas going forward. 
Chair Di Zazzo expressed a preference for flexible management of public comment 
as a discretion of the chair but acknowledged the utility of the 3-minute rule as a 
tool for preventing disruption.  Discussion was productive, but no formal vote was 
taken at this meeting. 
 
Roles & Responsibilities Document: 
 
Commissioner Sateriale moved to adopt the draft Roles & Responsibilities 
document distributed by Michelle Davidson.  As not all commissioners had yet had 
time to review the document, the vote was deferred.  Vote was deferred to the 
September 3, 2026 meeting to allow all members time to review. 
 
Zoom Disruption Procedures: 
 
Further clarification is needed on the Commission's authority to mute or remove 
disruptive remote participants from Zoom.   
 
9. OTHER BUINESS:
Page 8 
10. ADJOURN: 8:07 
There being no further business, a motion to adjourn was made by Seaman and 
seconded by Friant.  All in favor 
 
 
Respectfully submitted by, 
Dave Di Zazzo, Chair 
 
 
Respectfully submitted by: 
________________________ 
Michelle Davidson, Clerk 
Reviewed by: 
________________________ 
Kenneth Sateriale, Secretary 
Approved on: 
________________________
